triage_rationale: This is a COMPLEX task requiring full architectural redesign across 21+ files. Three critical failure domains: (1) Video/image media pipeline completely broken — video tab has zero frame extraction loop, camera handlers never instantiate MediaEngineService, image pipeline works but video path is a dead stub; (2) Full monochrome black/white redesign required — current design has 6 colorful ColorMode variants (matrix_green, amber, cyberpunk_neon, truecolor, rgb_ansi) that must all be stripped to pure B/W minimalism with professional graph/sticker aesthetic; (3) Load animation missing — only has 180ms CSS fade-in, needs a proper loading animation. Changes span React components, engine files, Rust backend, CSS, contracts, and type definitions. Architectural pattern changes: state management needs restructuring, styling engine must be fully redesigned, media pipeline must be rebuilt from scratch for video streaming.

conflicts_detected.description: Video streaming pipeline is completely dead. App.tsx handleSelectVideoFile (line 330-334) only sets a warning message and switches to the 'video' tab. There is NO video element, NO requestAnimationFrame loop reading video frames, and NO connection from video playback to the ASCII renderer. The 'video' mode in ControlPanel.tsx only has a file picker input but no video playback area or render loop.

Camera handlers never instantiate MediaEngineService. App.tsx handleStartCamera() (line 342) only sets isStreamingCamera=true and a warning string. It never calls mediaEngineService.startCamera(). Similarly handleStopCamera() only sets isStreamingCamera=false. The fully implemented MediaEngineService class in src/engine/media-service.ts is dead code in the current App.tsx.

Current design violates the monochrome black/white minimalism requirement. 6 ColorMode variants (matrix_green #00ff88, amber #ffb700, cyberpunk_neon #ff3366, truecolor RGB, rgb_ansi ANSI 16-color) are fully implemented and used throughout. primary #3B82F6 blue accent is in DARK_MINIMALIST_TOKENS, CSS custom properties, Tailwind config, and all range input accent colors. Must be stripped to pure #000000/#FFFFFF/#121212/#FAFAFA with 1px borders.

Load animation is missing. Only has 180ms mediaStateReveal CSS keyframe (opacity fade). The user explicitly requested a load animation when loading in the app interface. A proper loading spinner or progressive reveal animation must be implemented.

Duplicate renderer classes: src/engine/webgpu-renderer.ts and src/engine/webgl-renderer.ts are stubs that always fall back to renderImageDataToAscii (CPU), while src/lib/renderers/webgpu.ts and src/lib/renderers/webgl.ts contain the actual GPU shader implementations. This naming collision creates confusion and dead code.

video_image_failure_analysis:
VIDEO FAILURE: App.tsx handleSelectVideoFile (line 330-334) is a dead stub that only sets warningMessage and activeTab='video'. No video HTML element exists in the video mode. No requestAnimationFrame loop extracts frames from a video element. No connection from video playback to renderImageDataToAscii or renderProcedural3D. The ControlPanel.tsx video section (line 211-234) has a file input but no video playback area. The MediaPicker.tsx onApplyVideoElement prop exists but is never passed from App.tsx. The complete video-to-ASCII pipeline needs: (1) HTMLVideoElement rendering, (2) requestAnimationFrame frame extraction loop, (3) canvas capture of video frames, (4) ImageData conversion to ASCII via renderImageDataToAscii or Tauri IPC.

IMAGE FAILURE: Image handling partially works via handleSelectImageFile → preflightImageSource → rasterizeImageData → setAsciiOutput. However, the image flow has issues: (1) handleApplyPhotoToAscii requires a snapshotCanvas from MediaPicker which requires camera access that never initializes, (2) the image pipeline works but is buried in complex UI, (3) no image-to-ASCII preview exists before applying. The video pipeline is the critical failure — it's completely non-functional.

ROOT CAUSE: The media pipeline was designed with a MediaEngineService class but never wired it to the App component. handleStartCamera/handleStopCamera are stubs. The video tab was never implemented beyond a file picker. The MediaPicker's onApplyVideoElement and onApplyMediaStream callbacks are defined but never consumed by App.tsx or ControlPanel.
